title: Home's "Resume" restores a stale snapshot from boot over the match being played
problem: three facts each have their own home, and nothing keeps them in step: `hasSavedGame` is set once, by the read on mount (`:320`). Only `clearSavedGame` (reset) and the match-over render branch (`:337-340`) clear it. `savedRef` is also set once on mount (`:319`).
proposed: one owner for "is there a table to go back to", read from the live state first: The persist effect sets `savedRef.current` to what it writes, so the ref and storage cannot diverge. `hasSavedGame` becomes `resumable`, a derived value rather than state with its own setters.
effect: the flag state, its render-phase sync (`:336-340`) and the two set sites are removed. The bug class "Home offers a different table than the one in storage" is gone.

title: Online table teardown is written out by hand in three places, and the three lists disagree
problem: about 20 `useState`s and 10 refs make up "the table", but there is no single reset. Both `abandonRejoin` and `leaveRoom` clear: game state, room, seat, votes, disconnected seats, cumulative scores, `placementPointsCurrent`, the two exchange edge refs and the reconnect notice. Only `leaveRoom` also clears: `error`, `rejoiningRoomCodeRef`, `isSpectator`.
proposed: Better still, group the table fields into one `useState<TableRecord>` (or `useRef` plus setter), so a reset is `setTable(INITIAL_TABLE)` and a new field cannot be missed.
effect: about 45 hand-written reset lines become one call each. Bugs where one table's stale state shows on the next become structurally impossible.

title: Routing that follows table state is spread over five screens and three lobby-choice copies
problem: the interface is leaky. Each screen must know which transitions are "its own", whether to push or replace, and that it must key on `room?.roomId` rather than `room` (the comment is copied three times). Only the game screen consumes `rejoinFailed`, so a refusal that lands while another screen is up depends on the latch rule documented at `OnlineGameContext.tsx:141-147`.
proposed: A pure `placeFor({ room, hasGame, isSpectator, entrySource, rejoinFailed }): OnlinePlace` plus one `useOnlineRouting()` mounted in `app/(online)/_layout.tsx` that pushes or replaces on place change and consumes `rejoinFailed`.
effect: about 9 effects across 5 screens become one effect plus a pure function. Double navigation and missed transitions stop being per-screen concerns.

title: GameContext commands are render-scoped closures, so callers must manage freshness
problem: an unwritten rule of the interface: "a command is valid only for the render that produced it". Every timer-driven caller must know it. Two calls in one tick both compute from the same snapshot, which is a lost update instead of a refusal.
proposed: the same signatures, but stable identity, reading the latest state: or `useReducer` over engine transitions, with announcements emitted through F6's pure function.
effect: about 20 lines of ref plumbing in `app/game.tsx` go away. Stale-closure double application becomes impossible.

title: The slice hooks are pass-throughs; every field is declared six times and tests have two mock seams
problem: Deletion test: `export const useOnlineConnection = useConnectionSlice` behaves identically. The provider memo's deps are exactly the hook's deps, so the hook's object changes exactly when the slice's does. The local slices are a hypothetical seam: one context, so no render isolation (the file admits this, `contextSlices.test.ts:111`).
proposed: Make `onlineGameHooks.ts` a re-export of the provider's slice hooks (keeping the mocked import path), split `GameContext` into a rarely-changing `useLocalSession` context and a `useLocalTable` context, and add selector-sized reads such as `useIsWatching()`.
effect: about 170 lines out of `onlineGameHooks.ts`; `useOnlineGame` deleted, or moved to tests; `contextSlices.test.ts` partition checks become a type-level exclusivity assertion over the `Pick`s; Home and the online lobby stop re-rendering per move; one mock seam, or none with F11.
conflicts: CONTEXT.md: the six context slices are the seam, pinned by contextSlices.test.

title: The persisted table handles have no owner module; Home reads the storage key directly
problem: a missing seam. "Is there a table I can return to?" has no interface, and storage format and key ownership leak to a screen outside the provider's subtree.
proposed: Interface: export const tableHandles = { read(): Promise<{ activeRoomId: string|null; waitingCode: string|null }>;
effect: about 25 lines out of Home and about 20 out of the provider. The test stops mocking AsyncStorage.

title: Two different "accept an invite" paths
problem: one operation, two implementations with different preconditions.
proposed: `useInvites().accept(code)` (F8) as the only entry point. The friends screen calls it and navigates like Home does.
effect: one path, and `acceptInviteClearsPending.test.tsx` covers both callers.

title: Locale keys duplicate domain terms per screen, and the translations have already drifted
problem: CONTEXT.md says each domain term has one word that "each locale translates". The catalogue structure (namespaced by screen) means every new screen makes a new copy of a term, and nothing makes them agree.
proposed: a `term.*` namespace for glossary words (`term.mode.freeForAll`, `term.mode.teams`, `term.rank.queen`, `term.combo.straight`, …) plus tiny helpers `modeLabel(mode, t)` and `comboLabel(type, t)`. A test fails when a non-`term.*` key's English value equals a `term.*` value.
effect: about 20 keys times 3 locales removed and the drift fixed. Screens stop picking the per-screen key.

title: The server-error latch leaves "who clears it" to each screen
problem: `error` is set at `OnlineGameContext.tsx:546` and `621`. It is rendered four different ways: an inline banner (`(online)/index.tsx:241-258`), inline text (`quickmatch.tsx:264-266`), converted to a toast then cleared (`room.tsx:366-371`), and floated on the table (`game.tsx:276`). The provider clears it defensively on join, spectate and leave (`:934`, `942`, `975`, with comments about a standing error "greeting the player").
proposed: `error: { text; seq; surface: "lobby"|"table" } | null` with consumption tied to `seq` (`useServerError(surface)` acknowledges on read). Alternatively, fold it into F2's routing so the active place owns it. Category / effort / risk: in-process / S / low.
effect: about 12 lines removed across the four intents. The two `clearError()` calls in quickmatch.tsx are removed.

title: e2e configuration leaks into production interfaces
problem: `exchangeHoldMsOverride` is part of `GameContextValue` (`GameContext.tsx:120-121`, `161`), threaded through `useLocalExchange` and into `GameTable` (`app/game.tsx:233`). e2e knobs at module scope in `GameContext.tsx:48-67`. `process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_E2E_FAST === "1"` is evaluated at 14 sites across app, context, lib and components.
proposed: `GameTable`, or the exchange component, reads `e2e.exchangeHold` directly, and the field leaves the context interface. Category / effort / risk: in-process / S / low. The literal `process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_…` must stay greppable for inlining; one module does that.
effect: The two duplicate tests merge into one table test. Three literal-pin tests are deleted.

title: Small leaks in the auth and socket error modes
problem: `setSocketAuthFailureHandler`: a single global callback slot in `lib/socket.ts:39-42`, installed by a React provider (`SocketContext.tsx:288`, `474`). `AuthContext.logout` (`:195-200`) clears local state only after the POST succeeds. The auth-failure path (`SocketContext.tsx:286`) relies on it and navigates to `/auth` regardless, so a failed POST leaves the local session cached.
proposed: `connectSocket(userId, { onAuthFailure })`, held per socket; plus `AuthContext.forgetSession()` (local only), with `logout = server POST then forgetSession`, called with `finally`. Category / effort / risk: remote-owned / S / low.
effect: the cache and handles are partitioned by account rather than by the sign-out edge.

title: The HTTP API has no client module: keys, types and invalidation are spread out, with three fetch clients
problem: each caller must know the URL, the response type, which other keys go stale when, and which fetch to use. The query key is the URL (`query-client.ts:52`).
proposed: `lib/api.ts` with one `request<T>(method, route, body): Promise<Outcome<T>>` over `expo/fetch`, and `lib/queries.ts` with one typed entry per resource (`Q.friends`, `Q.statsMe`, …), `useApi(key)` and named invalidation sets (`stale.afterRound`, `onReconnect`, `afterFriendAccept`).
effect: 30 key literals and about 8 per-site type assertions removed; `fetchMe` and `fetchSocketTicket` shrink to about 3 lines each over `request`; one fetch implementation, so cookie and credential behaviour cannot diverge between login and every other call; invalidation sets named once, so a missed refresh after a round or friend event becomes a review of one table.

title: The offline "driver" lives in the screen, not in the offline adapter
problem: locality. Online, the counterpart of this code is the server. Offline, it is split between `GameContext` (engine transitions and persistence) and a route file.
proposed: The UI signals (`onExchangeReady`, `onRoundLanded`) still come from the table, so this is a hook rather than provider internals.
effect: `app/game.tsx` drops from 238 to about 90 lines and becomes a pure props mapping like the online screen. The driver gets a `renderHook` test surface with fake timers, so the six screen tests above can assert driver behaviour without `GameTable`.

title: Exchange-announcement detection is implemented twice, differently
problem: one concept ("an exchange just resolved, or the two-Joker exception was dealt") has two derivations. The engine already provides everything the online path reads: `processExchangeChoice` sets `cardToLoser` (`lib/game/gameEngine.ts:968`).
proposed: Both adapters call it from their single commit path: `commitState` offline, `onGameState` online.
effect: two refs and four reset lines deleted online; offline announce code moves out of the commands. One pure test table covers both transports, replacing parts of `exchangeAnnounceBothWays`, `exchangeAnnounceFrame` and `ceremonyHoldsTheCard`.
notes: 03-app-context: partially addressed by commit 4475dd2e (offline announces only after the engine accepts the give, GameContext.tsx:233-234); the two derivations (command time offline, state diff online) remain.

title: SocketContext mixes four responsibilities and hands screens the raw socket
problem: a god context with a shallow, leaky surface. Every `useSocket()` consumer (Home, the online lobby, friends, room, and `OnlineGameProvider` itself) re-renders on every `friend:status` presence change.
proposed: Split into `useConnection()` (lifecycle only), `usePresence()`, and `useInvites()` with named `accept`/`dismiss`/`send` commands; friends cache sync becomes a listener hook in lib/friends.ts and `qc.clear()` on sign-out moves to AuthContext.
effect: no screen holds `socket`, so the 3 raw emits move behind named commands with error feedback; presence churn wakes only presence readers; the 20 tests mocking `@/context/SocketContext` each mock one small surface; dead `connected` deleted.

title: OnlineGameContext as a whole is a god provider (map of where F1, F6, F7, F9 and F14 apply)
problem: `context/OnlineGameContext.tsx` (about 1140 lines) holds surface types and slices, persisted handles, a rejoin state machine, connection status, the protocol-version gate, room and game state, banners, match results and query invalidation, votes, reactions, disconnect notices, intents and teardown.
proposed: Extract by responsibility while keeping effects in place: `useRejoin(socket, handles, onRefused)` plus client-F1 `endTable`, F6 `exchangeAnnounceFor`, F7 `stale.afterRound` and F9 `tableHandles`. No `reduce(state, event)`.
effect: the provider drops from about 1140 to about 700 lines. The rejoin rules (the stale-reply guard, the retry cap of 3 at 2000 ms) get a `renderHook` plus fake-socket test surface of their own instead of being exercised through the full provider (`rejoinFailed.test.tsx`).
notes: Respects the CONTEXT.md 2026-09-10 rejection of a reduce(state, event) extraction; this is a map of F1/F6/F7/F9.

title: Account deletion is reported as failed after it succeeded
problem: the DELETE succeeds and the server destroys the session (routes.ts:796-800). The modal then calls `onClose()` and `await logout()`. `logout` POSTs `/api/auth/logout` before it clears local state (AuthContext.tsx:195-200).
proposed: keep only the DELETE inside the try. On success, clear the session locally and skip the server logout.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: The room's bots-countdown re-renders the whole screen every second for every viewer
problem: non-hosts, and rooms that are not waiting, re-render `RoomScreen` (seat list, invite panel, `FlatList`) 30 times for a hint they never see.
proposed: move the countdown into a `BotsComingHint` child, mounted only when `hostIsWaiting`, which owns its interval. `botsOffered` comes up through `onDue`.
effect: 30 whole-screen renders per room visit become 30 renders of one `Text`.

title: useOwnLink resets the shared link edges on every subscribe
problem: `edgesOf.set(socket, NO_LINK)` runs on each subscribe against a WeakMap shared per socket. A second subscriber, or a resubscribe during an outage, erases `downAt`, so the outage duration restarts. There is only one caller today, so the defect is latent.
proposed: initialise only when the entry is missing (`if (!edgesOf.has(socket))`).
effect: correct outage timing under any number of subscribers.

title: Connection status is three subscriptions plus a composition in the screen
problem: Connection status is three subscriptions plus a composition in the screen: `connected` via `useSyncExternalStore` (OnlineGameContext.tsx:346-361), `useOwnLink(socket)` subscribing to the same events again (lib/useOwnLink.ts:23-56), a dead `connected` state in SocketContext, and `app/(online)/game.tsx` composing `linkPill(...)` into a `ConnectionNote`.
proposed: `useOnlineConnection()` returns `connectionNote: ConnectionNote | null` (built once, from the pure `lib/ownLink.ts`), plus `ownLink`.
effect: about 20 lines out of the screen. The pill mapping becomes a unit test instead of a screen test (`onlineStatusRow`, `tableNotices` connection cases).

title: Error-toast boilerplate repeated
problem: `showNotification({ type: "game_error", title: t("common.error"), message })` at `friends.tsx:67`, `room.tsx:368`, `room.tsx:404`, `OnlineGameContext.tsx:902-907`, `SocketContext.tsx:424-429` and `443-448`. The last two are identical bodies. Proposed interface: `notifyError(message: string)` on `NotificationContext`, and `notifyServerError(payload)`.
proposed: `notifyError(message: string)` on `NotificationContext`, and `notifyServerError(payload)`.
effect: 6 sites become 1 line each. Category / effort / risk: in-process / S / none.

title: NotificationContext mixes a stable command with fast-changing state
problem: `context/NotificationContext.tsx:96-105`. A single value holds `showNotification` (stable) together with `notification` and `bannerBottom`, so every component that only calls `showNotification` (both online providers, `GameProvider`, room, friends, SettingsModal) re-renders on every banner change and every measured `bannerBottom`. Proposed interface: split into a `NotifyContext` (`showNotification`, `notifyError`) and a `BannerContext` (`notification`, `dismiss`, `bannerBottom`, `report`).
proposed: split into a `NotifyContext` (`showNotification`, `notifyError`) and a `BannerContext` (`notification`, `dismiss`, `bannerBottom`, `report`). `useBannerBottom` already reads separately. Category / effort / risk: in-process / S / low.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: Stored settings JSON is parsed twice
problem: the format has two readers, and only one validates. Not proposed: CONTEXT.md's "Feedback master state" note rejects a single `applyFeedbackSettings`; this keeps the separate setters.
proposed: `lib/settingsStore.ts`: `export function readStoredSettings(): Promise<Partial<Settings>>` (moving `parseStored` there), used by both. Category / effort / risk: local-substitutable / S / low.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.
notes: Respects the CONTEXT.md feedback-master-state decision (no applyFeedbackSettings).

title: The query loading / error / data block is repeated about 10 times
problem: `app/profile.tsx:587-596`, `630-634`, `747-753`, `797-800`; `leaderboard.tsx` (7 `LoadingBlock`/`ErrorBlock`/retry sites); `history.tsx` (4); `friends.tsx` (5); `room.tsx:249-255`; `replay.tsx`. Proposed interface: Category / effort / risk: in-process / S / low. The `stale` and empty variants differ per site, so they must remain props.
proposed: Category / effort / risk: in-process / S / low. The `stale` and empty variants differ per site, so they must remain props.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: Room-code normalisation is scattered and the two join commands disagree
problem: `OnlineGameContext.tsx:943` (`spectateRoom` uppercases), `:927-936` (`joinRoom` does not), `(online)/index.tsx:128`, `135`, `369`, `lib/deepLink.ts:4-8` (`joinCode`). Proposed interface: `joinRoom` and `spectateRoom` both normalise through `joinCode()`; callers pass raw input. Category / effort / risk: in-process / S / none.
proposed: `joinRoom` and `spectateRoom` both normalise through `joinCode()`; callers pass raw input. Category / effort / risk: in-process / S / none.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: The tutorial route file holds pure content and engine validation
problem: `app/tutorial.tsx:40-454` (card literals, `buildExchangeState`, `buildBeats` at about 180 lines, `stageBeat`, `evaluatePlay`, `evaluateExchange`). Progress persistence is inline AsyncStorage at `:477-506`. Proposed interface: `lib/tutorial/beats.ts`: `buildBeats(t): Beat[]`, `evaluatePlay(sel, beat, t)`, `evaluateExchange(card, beat, t)`; plus `tutorialProgress.{read,write,clear}` beside `lib/tutorialSeen.ts`.
proposed: `lib/tutorial/beats.ts`: `buildBeats(t): Beat[]`, `evaluatePlay(sel, beat, t)`, `evaluateExchange(card, beat, t)`; plus `tutorialProgress.{read,write,clear}` beside `lib/tutorialSeen.ts`.
effect: the screen drops from about 900 to about 450 lines. The validation becomes unit-testable under `node --test`; today `tutorialTableBeats.test.tsx` renders the screen.

title: Contexts store translated strings, not payloads
problem: the providers depend on i18n (presentation), and a language switch in SettingsModal does not re-render a standing error or notice. `useTranslation().translateServerPayload` exists (`lib/i18n.ts:185-192`) but the contexts cannot use it.
proposed: store `{ payload: ServerPayload; seq }` and translate at render. Category / effort / risk: in-process / S / low. A cosmetic edge, not a priority bug.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: `tn()` takes an untyped base string
problem: `lib/i18n.ts:136-141` (`base: string`, then `as TranslationKey`). A misspelled base compiles; `tests/ui-rules/i18n.test.ts:776-782` only checks for unused keys. Proposed interface: ``type PluralBase = { [K in TranslationKey]: K extends `${infer B}_one` ?
proposed: ``type PluralBase = { [K in TranslationKey]: K extends `${infer B}_one` ? B : never }[TranslationKey]; tn(base: PluralBase, …)``
effect: about 14 call sites become compile-checked. Category / effort / risk: in-process / S / none.

title: The rating summary is written twice, and provisionality is derived on both sides of the wire
problem: app/profile.tsx:599-614 and app/(online)/leaderboard.tsx:37-42, 57-68 (the same season/rounds strings and the same a11y group); app/(online)/game.tsx:208-218 (`provisionalLeft` recomputed from `rounds < PROVISIONAL_ROUNDS`); server/game/ratings.ts:197 (the server's own `provisional: rounds < PROVISIONAL_ROUNDS`, sent on `RatingDto` but not on `RatingAfter`). proposed: `lib/game/rating.ts: provisionalLeft(r: { rounds: number }): number | undefined` used by the server's flag and by all three screens, plus …
proposed: `lib/game/rating.ts: provisionalLeft(r: { rounds: number }): number | undefined` used by the server's flag and by all three screens, plus `components/RatingSummary.tsx({ rating: RatingDto })` used by profile and leaderboard.
effect: about 30 duplicated lines removed. The provisional threshold is read through one function.

title: Lobby pickers are copied across three screens, and two restate the teams rule with a literal 4
problem: app/(online)/room.tsx:142-177 (`MatchLengthControls`, "Mirrors the offline lobby's picker") = app/lobby.tsx:131-134, 246-262; player-count chips app/(online)/index.tsx:169-182 = app/lobby.tsx:212-224; teams-needs-four as a literal at app/(online)/index.tsx:184, 195-196 and app/lobby.tsx:170, 226, while app/(online)/room.tsx:383-384 and server/socket/socketTable.ts:133 use `TEAMS_PLAYER_COUNT`. proposed: `components/MatchLengthPicker({ value, onChange, seats })` and `SeatCountPicker`, plus `modeFits(mode, …
proposed: `components/MatchLengthPicker({ value, onChange, seats })` and `SeatCountPicker`, plus `modeFits(mode, seats): boolean` exported next to `TEAMS_PLAYER_COUNT` in the engine, used by all three screens and the server.
effect: 3 inventory duplicate blocks removed. A change to the teams seat count reaches every screen.

title: Reduce-motion opens one native subscription per subscriber
problem: on native, `subscribeSystemReduceMotion` adds an `AccessibilityInfo` listener and fires an `isReduceMotionEnabled()` bridge call for every subscriber. Every CardView subscribes, so one table mount opens about 54 native listeners and bridge calls for one boolean.
proposed: a module store with one native listener, ref-counted, and a cached value. `useSyncExternalStore` readers share it, following the pattern already used for the in-app setting in the same file.
effect: one listener per app; no bridge burst on deal.
